key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers, delivering 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with lead-halide perovskite cells.
engineering_relevance: Improved carrier extraction in thicker AgBiS2 nanocrystal films supports stronger near-infrared harvesting for stable, scalable thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange for one-step deposition of passivated, thicker nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-light-absorbing perovskite cells in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention for AgBiS2 cells after three months in dry air without encapsulation.
watch_item: The >47.5% triple-junction efficiency is a modeled potential, not a demonstrated device result; storage stability also does not establish operational durability.
paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
